The Counter
Every step grew the dealer first. The counter is the next dot.
Steel made him a supplier. Lighting made him a showroom. Fans and wires made him a one-stop counter. Each time Surya invested in the dealer before asking anything of him — and each time the counter carried more of the business.
So why has that counter never been upgraded?
02

Four links modernised. The fifth is still printed and pasted.
Surya already runs ordering, distribution, payments and schemes on digital rails. Only the last three feet — where the customer actually decides — still runs on a board that cannot be changed after the day it goes up.
If it is the obvious gap, why has nobody closed it?

The concept

One unit. Four ways to reach the customer.

01

TFT video screen

Runs the Surya brand film on loop from the moment the counter opens.

02

Lit SURYA logo

White edge-lit acrylic on the orange body. Visible across the shop, on even when the screen sleeps.

03

Three product models

Wires, Lighting and Fans. Each sits on a button — press it and that product's film plays.

04

Catalogue QR

The customer scans, the full catalogue opens on their phone. They leave with Surya in hand.

Know our products just in a click of a button.

No menu, no instructions, nothing to learn. A customer curious about a cable box simply presses it — and that product’s film plays. It is the most natural interaction there is on a shop counter, because the thing being touched is the product itself, not a picture of one. And because the switch is sealed and mechanical, it survives the dust, grease and rough handling that would finish a touch panel.

360° view

Turn it around. Change the size.

The screen is live — the brand film loops on its own. Click any of the three products and watch that product's film take over, exactly as a customer would at the counter. Drag to spin a full 360°, and switch sizes or orientation — the whole body re-proportions, because every size is drawn to its real dimensions.

Tip — click a product on the unit to trigger its film. Drag anywhere to rotate.

Sizes

Three sizes, shown to scale.

Counter space varies enormously between a wholesale market shop and a metro showroom. Same layout, same lit logo, same three product pods and QR across all three.

What plays, and who controls it.

Default loop

Brand film, new launches, dealer schemes, festive campaigns. Runs whenever nobody is interacting.

Three product films

Wires, Lighting and Fans — each triggered by its own button and played in full.

Central control

All units connect over the dealer's Wi-Fi. Content pushes from one dashboard. Screens keep playing the last synced content if the internet drops.

Central control

One dashboard. Every counter. Any campaign.

What the console can do

💬
THE DIFFERENCE The counter starts talking back

Every press and every QR scan is a customer telling Surya what they came in for — by product, by city, by season. A board can only speak. This listens.

📤
Publish once, everywhere

One upload lands on every counter the same evening. No dealer visit, no courier, no reprint.

🎯
Target precisely

All counters, or by state, city, screen size, dealer tier or a named outlet list.

📅
Schedule ahead

Load Diwali in September, set the date, forget it. Dayparting for peak counter hours.

🌐
Regional language

Bengali in West Bengal, Hindi in UP and Bihar — same campaign, one schedule.

📡
Live fleet health

Who is online, what is playing, who has gone dark — with alerts before the dealer calls.

📈
Proof of play

What ran, where, how many times. Auditable reporting for every rupee of the branding budget.

📶
Works offline

If the shop Wi-Fi drops, the screen keeps playing the last synced content and re-syncs later.

👤
Roles and approvals

National marketing publishes; zonal managers see only their region; every push is logged and reversible.

⚡
Emergency override

A price revision or recall notice reaches every counter in minutes, not weeks.

📷
Install verification

GPS-tagged photo, commissioning date, dealer sign-off and warranty mapped to each serial.

🔑
Surya-branded, Surya-owned

Your logo, your colours, your web address. The dealer sees Surya, not a vendor.

Why this matters more than the screen

A printed board is a one-time spend that decays. A connected counter is something Surya can change on Monday for a scheme and on Friday for a festival — and that sends back what customers actually asked about. The screen is the hardware. This is the asset.
